name: Inquisitor
focus: Trace what makes a claim hold.

skills.name: Reading the evidence

steps.action: Separate the kinds of dates on two pens
Hold the pen or surface steady while comparing marks
Distinguish an independent observer from a repeated slip
Leave a reference another crew can check

skills.task: A blue label at the hall says a pen always makes a clean line. Two practice strips share a surface. A third comes from a different paper.

choices.label: Clip the two matching surfaces
choices.result: Dace puts the matched strips in one sleeve. The next visitor can compare the pen marks while the surface stays steady.

choices.label: Raise the third strip on its own foot
choices.result: Venn fits a separate mount. People can see where the extra paper is useful and keep its test conditions in view.

skills.name: Building a case

steps.action: Use a dated record to make the first exhibit label hold
Follow a claim through a trader, a ledger and a workshop
Try both sides of a proposal before settling the next turn
Publish the new rule with the waiting job still visible

skills.task: The Guild repair line can reach the street. The old notice promises a new part. The bill of work records only a cleaned one.

choices.label: Put the work slip below the claim
choices.result: Venn gives visitors the original wording and the slip together. A reader can narrow the promise to this repair.

choices.label: Leave a hook for a second repair bill
choices.result: Dace gives the waiting guild a place to bring a documented exception. The promise stays tied to the work already done.

skills.name: Finding a missing view

steps.action: Track the reader the loan count leaves out
Make both ends of the aisle usable from the same drawing
Check what the dispatch tally misses from each route
Give new library readers an actual way to get counted

skills.task: The case-room tally counts tickets from the entry desk. Wren’s late readers walk in by the far rail without passing it.

choices.label: Set a second tally at the far rail
choices.result: The next round can show how many people come past each tally. Venn leaves the two collection places printed beside the counts.

choices.label: Ask the keepers to trace one complete round
choices.result: Dace sends a keeper along both approaches with a clean tally. The old tickets remain available as a record of the first desk.

question: What makes a claim hold up when someone tests it?

name: Oracle
focus: Set the limits of an automatic tool.

skills.name: Choosing and directing a tool

steps.action: Compare the whole page and the narrow viewer
Run the pattern bench with two differently selected sets
Test changed rule on the same combined library records
Keep documented model conditions beside the result for its next reader

skills.task: The Dispatch Clerk can tune a copy to fit a notice or carry it to a handover. The short copy fits the slot, but drops the start point.

choices.label: Keep the named start before shortening the copy
choices.result: Lin can use the copying tool for the narrow public slot. The start remains legible beside the turn.

choices.label: Send the full route and add a separate turn strip
choices.result: Ade puts the full route on the wider review table. The tool drafts a strip for the turn while the source remains within reach.

skills.name: Auditing an automatic result

steps.action: Keep missing requests in view when the count changes
Compare two rules without switching their examples
Check the answer against a reserved case
Test a proposed schedule after the load changes

skills.task: A route rule worked for daytime slips. Ade has one late carrier whose request was set aside before the rule was fitted.

choices.label: Run the unused slip on the old rule
choices.result: Ade adds the outcome on its own slip. The crew can see the difference between the fitting examples and the late carrier’s check.

choices.label: Ask a second keeper to try the same rule
choices.result: Lin records the second keeper’s result and the slips that went into it. The label keeps the test small enough to repeat.

skills.name: Setting limits with people

steps.action: Keep the permission slip near the door decision
Set the copying bench’s consent and source boundaries
Deliver only the approved extract for readers
Use the checked bench result to make a public choice with limits

skills.task: A box can copy a doorstep instruction from two older notes. The keepers have permission to share only the second note with the waiting queue.

choices.label: Feed in the approved line and credit its carrier
choices.result: Lin gives the queue a short instruction with its source. The first note stays in the keeper’s closed case.

choices.label: Leave room for the carrier to speak
choices.result: Ade marks a time for the carrier’s approved directions. The machine guide lists where listeners can ask about its scope.

question: Where should an automatic tool stop, and a person decide?

name: Empath
focus: Find how other people come to a view.

skills.name: Seeing from another position

steps.action: Help two people reach the same case from opposite approaches
Use different observers’ lower and upper records
Stand at the two approaches after reading a carrier’s reply
Leave directions that begin where each reader arrives

skills.task: A carrier from the quay sees the lamp behind a railing. A reader from the stairs sees it above the welcome bench.

choices.label: Hang an approach card where each person arrives
choices.result: Wren hangs separate approach cards. The top line on either card names its own place of arrival.

choices.label: Mark the first landmark they can both see
choices.result: Eren signals from a point both paths can reach. The copy sends each reader to the same named corner.

skills.name: Carrying words between communities

steps.action: Leave a route note someone at the ferry can trace
Give a shore name its own place and crew
Compare what each guide preserves about the local phrase
Keep both dates in reach at the source chosen by its readers

skills.task: Wren’s route word includes the custom of stopping to wait at a lamp. A visiting courier needs to know where to stop before unloading.

choices.label: Keep the word with a guide to the stop
choices.result: Wren keeps the route word above the waiting place. The guide gives the courier an action without taking the word away from its users.

choices.label: Lead with the delivery cue and link to Wren’s wording
choices.result: Eren hangs the short action at the unloading point. The reader can follow the source back to the fuller wording.

skills.name: Following consequences together

steps.action: Put the packed copy in the hands of a reader
Follow people whose work depends on the other channel
Open one service and check who reaches it
Carry a public allocation with the waiting requests still attached

skills.task: Moving the public bench off the quay shields its readers from wind. The lamp mark can then disappear for people at the far stairs.

choices.label: Keep the bench and add a sheltered guide
choices.result: Wren leaves the queue where the lamp can be seen. An extra route strip comes inside for readers who want shelter.

choices.label: Move the bench and keep a light on the landing
choices.result: Eren opens the sheltered reading space. The quay light still shows the turn to carriers coming down the far stairs.

question: How do other people come to see things the way they do?

name: Chronicler
focus: Return to a decision with better information.

skills.name: Rechecking an earlier inference

steps.action: Open the note that leaves room for a second check
Change a date ribbon after a person tries it
Revise after a reader misinterprets an empty square
Leave an independent reference for a new Guardian

skills.task: The Ferry yard’s first blue line looks like yesterday’s mark. Two pages nearby use a different starting edge.

choices.label: Lay tomorrow’s empty slip beside the first reading
choices.result: Hesper keeps an open place for tomorrow and notes the edge the first reading used.

choices.label: Set the two edges side by side
choices.result: Kip can compare where the two measurements started before filing a correction.

skills.name: Planning and adapting a search

steps.action: Put a found object on record with its owner line open
Use the original place and a related record to follow the blade
Match the gauge to a jig and then check the gift record
Finish a handover with room for another person’s verification

skills.task: Kip has time for a close look at one cabinet before a handoff. Hesper can do the other check when the case reaches the workshop.

choices.label: Put the match check first and carry the open question
choices.result: Kip sets the gauge beside the matching slot. The case arrives with the outstanding date question attached.

choices.label: Trace the loan number first and leave space for fit
choices.result: Hesper gets the located loan slip and a place to add the fit check. The case has an assigned next keeper.

skills.name: Learning from a changed result

steps.action: Try a new mounting after the ferry print slips
Repeat the rainfall check at the next bell
Repeat a drought setting after the gate repair
Publish the old and new results with their separate conditions

skills.task: The repaired hook holds the same case higher. The old damage report still matters when another keeper asks when the scrape appeared.

choices.label: Hang both checks with their different hook settings
choices.result: Hesper can find the older scrape and the new clearance on the same board, each beside its own setup.

choices.label: Keep a live repair label, with the old report clipped behind
choices.result: Kip uses the repaired route today. Pulling the clip brings back the earlier scrape and the hook it belonged to.

question: When better information arrives, how should we look again at a decision already made?

name: Weaver
focus: Help other people use what they found.

skills.name: Making a complex account usable

steps.action: Give a reader the patent detail and a path to the whole sheet
Build a strip that can lead a reader to its source
Set a proof format for late readers at the theatre
Give the trial loading limit and the route their own lines

skills.task: Leila’s relief copy can fit one prominent phrase. A walker needs a turn, and a keeper needs the leaf behind the phrase.

choices.label: Put the turn in large type, with its leaf number
choices.result: A walker can act on the large line. Leila gives the keeper the drawer number directly below.

choices.label: Open the two-part proof at both lines
choices.result: Marek sets the proof where a carrier can read from the bench. The short cue and full wording are both in reach.

skills.name: Keeping a conversation useful

steps.action: Hear both speakers before the practice Showdown
Ask two record keepers what ties an object to a scribe
Check the full instruction with the person who uses the other approach
Make the next notice with the listener’s reading in view

skills.task: Leila says a door is closed while the peg is being checked. A new runner has heard the word as an order to leave.

choices.label: Have the runner say what they heard before posting
choices.result: Leila asks the runner to show the next turn. They change the waiting line where it will affect the walk.

choices.label: Post the two requests with Leila’s brief explanation
choices.result: The rail shows where to wait and where to go. Readers can raise another question with both readings in sight.

skills.name: Joining different people’s work

steps.action: Try a case handle and see how it holds for a carrier
Coordinate a proposed correction with another messenger
Follow the calls and signed record through a crew handover
Set a joined handover where the next crew uses it

skills.task: The archive runners can make their own route check. The person on the bench keeps better track of where a copy has gone.

choices.label: Send two slips with a shared arrival mark
choices.result: Marek takes the route slip and Leila takes the copy receipt. Both can trace the handover by its marked arrival.

choices.label: Clip the receiver’s copy to the runner’s check
choices.result: Leila gives the next crew one linked pack. Separate signatures keep both people’s jobs readable.

question: How can what one person found become useful to someone else?
